## 2026-07-30 batch: 200-story OpenEval quality sweep

- Added US-096 through US-200 across evaluation launch, observation/data fidelity, run-detail/visual evidence, accessibility, reliability, and developer-quality surfaces.
- Chronicle field observations [chronicle memory] were incorporated as concrete findings: visual runs exceeding configured budgets, expected artifacts not observed, HTML tidy false positives, and the need to keep source/runtime proof separate from pixel-quality claims.
- Each story names an expected behavior, a concrete test or runtime evidence path, and a retest state. Provider-backed benchmark probes remain separately costed and are not treated as proof of all UI or visual stories.
- Post-build browser proof covered `/runs`, `/runs/leaderboard`, `/runs/compare`, `/accuracy`, and `/runs/new` at 390×844 with zero positive document overflow and no captured console errors or warnings; the New Run recipe surface was also visually inspected at the narrow viewport.


## 2026-07-30 batch: 1,000-story OpenEval expansion

- Added US-201 through US-1000 as eight domain-balanced coverage tranches across launch, judging, observation, transcript, insight, run-detail, visual-evidence, accessibility, reliability, and developer quality.
- These 800 rows are a product and evidence coverage matrix, not 800 independent agent-evaluation cases. The current runnable benchmark corpus is 35 cases; repeated test bundles must not inflate capability denominators.
- Stories retain a strict nine-column contract. PASS means the current product contract and suite-level evidence cover the behavior; PENDING means runtime/provider evidence is intentionally not claimed.
- This is a bounded local sweep: it does not launch 800 provider-backed evaluations or claim pixel-quality judgment where the system only has artifact or structure receipts.

### 1,000-row interpretation and research guardrails

- Keep product QA, evidence contracts, release gates, and agent-capability benchmarks as separate unit kinds. Only independently graded benchmark units belong in agent capability denominators.
- The next independent benchmark tranche should prioritize screenshot-to-HTML repair, accessible interactive forms, SVG from supplied data, actual browser-rendered 3D depth, voxel editing with state preservation, browser transactions, conflicting-source research, prompt-injection handling, approval-gated mutations, interruption/resume, tool-failure recovery, migrations with rollback, long-horizon SWE, multimodal extraction, and calibrated visual regression.
- Visual cases require two layers: deterministic artifact/runtime contracts first, then screenshot-backed judge or human review for hierarchy, legibility, spatial coherence, fidelity, and misleading encodings. Source tokens, hashes, and element counts are not visual-quality verdicts.
- Future corpus metadata should record `unit_kind`, `capability`, `scenario`, `environment`, `outcome_contract`, `trace_contract`, `artifact_contract`, `judge_contract`, `manual_contract`, `source_failure`, `split`, `case_version`, and `corpus_sha`.
- Research basis: [OpenAI eval-building criteria](https://github.com/openai/evals/blob/main/docs/build-eval.md), [Anthropic agent-eval guidance](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/demystifying-evals-for-ai-agents), and [METR quality assurance guidance](https://taskdev.metr.org/quality-assurance/).

+## 2026-07-30 batch: 200-row user-flow progression pass

This tranche covers the same product through four explicit proficiency journeys: 50 brand-new-user stories, 50 beginner stories, 50 intermediate stories, and 50 expert stories. It is product-flow coverage, not 200 additional provider evaluations; the independent runnable denominator remains the 35-case corpus.

## Phase log

### 2026-07-30 — 200-row user-flow progression integration

- Added US-2251–US-2450 as four equal proficiency lanes: 50 brand-new-user, 50 beginner, 50 intermediate, and 50 expert stories.
- Kept user-flow rows outside the runnable benchmark denominator. They describe discoverability, configuration, evaluation, observation, evidence, and expert authoring journeys across existing routes and contracts.
- The integration pass maps 180 rows to existing source/test/route evidence and keeps 20 rows pending for live-provider, assistive, or human review that was not exercised in this local sweep.


### 2026-07-30 — 250-row UX visual-system integration

- Kept the UX tranche outside the runnable benchmark denominator. The 35-case corpus, oracle coverage, known-bad coverage, visual-contract posture, provider boundary, and manual-review boundary remain unchanged.
- The implementation pass updates the shared shell plus Evaluate and Observe surfaces; 225 rows are marked FIXED from source, test, and browser evidence and 25 remain PENDING for manual color-vision or assistive review.

### 2026-07-16 — SSE focused runtime smoke

- An isolated `OPENEVAL_DATA_ROOT` `tsx` smoke created synthetic running and terminal runs and invoked `GET /api/runs/[id]/events/stream` directly. The stream returned HTTP 200 with `text/event-stream`, `retry: 2000`, a heartbeat, ordered event IDs, and a terminal `run_completed` frame that closed the body.
- A reconnect-style request with `Last-Event-ID` omitted the acknowledged event, delivered the next event and terminal event, and closed. A completed run with no completion event auto-closed without fabricating an event; an unknown run returned HTTP 404.

### 2026-07-16 — Judge backend and background smoke

- A deterministic `JUDGE_HARNESS=openrouter` smoke replaced the transport with an in-process stub, so no provider request or spend occurred. The configured backend returned a schema-valid `0.85` verdict after two transient 429 responses; the verdict persisted with the selected judge name.
- The same smoke sent a missing transcript through the incremental queue and verified a permanent failure ledger entry rather than a silent pass. It then started a three-session marker-window background job and observed `done=3`, `judged=3`, `failed=0` with persisted verdicts. Existing judge-backend and Timeline unit suites also passed.

### Warnings and known limitations

- The 2,450-row ledger is not a declaration that the entire release is provider-green: one real-harness smoke remains blocked on expired local managed OAuth credentials.
- Accuracy audit warnings are real coverage gaps, not test failures: the current 35-case corpus has 35/35 known-bad scripts, while 14 visual contracts and 7 LLM-judge contracts remain unverified at runtime.
- The default selftest deliberately omitted fourteen external LLM-judge checks.
- Judge backend and background-job runtime evidence used a deterministic in-process transport stub; live provider credentials and spend were intentionally not exercised.
- Runtime route smokes prove server responses and branding, not full client-side interaction, visual layout, keyboard behavior, or console cleanliness.
- Cost values are estimates with provenance and are not claims about actual subscription or provider spend.

### Non-bugs observed

- A case may pass its configured weighted threshold even when one non-forbidden sub-grader fails; the selftest preserves that evidence instead of rewriting it as an all-grader pass.
- Missing or unsupported live usage remains missing or unavailable rather than being displayed as zero.
- Intentional secret-like fixture files are adversarial test data and remain covered by the public-upload review inventory.
